units.titleZh: 數字與時間 × 語言與句型

passages.title: Numbers and Time: First Reading
passages.text: Our English class starts at eleven a.m. Every student brings a short story to read. Mia reads with me because she feels nervous. After an hour, our teacher asks us about one new word: "true." We explain where we found it and why it matters in the story. When the class ends, Mia smiles. She says reading with a friend made the morning easier. We plan to practice again in the afternoon. I happily agree.

passages.title: Language Tools: Second Reading
passages.text: Two hours ago, Grandpa called and invited me to his house. I went there after my afternoon class and stayed until the evening. We talked about the town where he grew up. He told me why he loved the old library and showed me a book with his name in it. I asked, "Is every story in this book true?" Grandpa laughed and said some were true, but others came from his imagination. We will read more next week.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: When should we meet for our English project?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: How about eleven a.m. in the library?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I have music class then. Can we meet in the afternoon?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sure. Where do you want to sit?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's use the table by the window.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good idea. We can work for about an hour.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Why don't we bring our word cards too?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, and we can practice them together.

units.titleZh: 人物與家庭 × 數字與時間
units.titleEn: People and Family & Numbers and Time

passages.title: People and Family: First Reading
passages.text: Yesterday morning, my aunt and uncle came to our house at nine o'clock. My uncle is a factory worker, and he usually starts work very early. He had a free day, so our whole family ate breakfast together. Dad made eggs while my aunt cut fruit for the children. My little cousin is still a young child, but she helped carry the cups. After breakfast, Daddy took a family photo, and everyone smiled. They stayed until after lunch.

passages.title: Numbers and Time: Second Reading
passages.text: Our school sports day started at two p.m. yesterday. My friend Ben came with his family, including his aunt, uncle, and two children. His dad helped at the starting line, and my daddy gave water to the runners. At three o'clock, the relay race began. Our team had zero points at first, but we did not give up. We ran carefully and finished second. Every child cheered, and the adults clapped for us. We talked about it all afternoon.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Dad, what time does the family picnic start?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It starts at ten o'clock tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are Aunt May and Uncle Sam coming?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, and they are bringing the children.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can I invite my friend Leo too?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Of course. His family can join us.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Great! I will call him before eight p.m.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. Please help Daddy pack the food first.

units.titleZh: 動物與自然 × 身體與感受
units.titleEn: Animals and Nature & Body and Feelings

passages.title: Animals and Nature: First Reading
passages.text: Our class visited a small farm when the weather was cool. I fed a brown horse with my hand and watched a duck swim across the pond. The horse moved its head close to my bag because it could smell my lunch. I felt nervous at first, but its soft hair tickled my arm. Soon my whole body relaxed. By noon, I was hungry too, so I ate under a tree and drew each animal with chalk.

passages.title: Body and Feelings: Second Reading
passages.text: A strong wind blew through the park, so Nina and I took out our kite. She held it above her head while I ran across the grass. The kite climbed high, but the string rubbed my hand and made it sore. We stopped because I did not feel well. After a short rest and a drink, I felt better. The evening weather became calm, and the first star appeared. We packed the kite into its bag and walked home.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Look at that duck near the pond!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It is hiding its head under its wing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Do you think the animal is hungry?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Maybe, but the sign says we should not feed it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The weather is getting windy now.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then let's put our chalk and pictures in the bag.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can we fly our kite before we leave?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sure, but hold the string tightly in your hand.

units.titleZh: 食物與用餐 × 校園與學習
units.titleEn: Food and Meals & School and Learning

passages.title: Food and Meals: First Reading
passages.text: Our class had a breakfast lesson in the school kitchen. We used a computer to read a simple recipe for banana cookies. I wrote each step in my notebook, but I made a spelling mistake and used my eraser. Then our teacher showed us how to measure and mix the food. While the cookies baked, we learned how heat changes the dough. At the end, everyone ate one cookie and had a drink of water.

passages.title: School and Learning: Second Reading
passages.text: I helped Dad prepare dinner while my sister finished her homework. Dad cooked beef and vegetables, and I made cold drinks for everyone. My sister came into the kitchen to ask how to spell "banana" for a story. I wrote the word on a small board, but she erased it and tried again by herself. After we ate, she used the computer to show us what she had learned. Then we shared two cookies for dessert.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What are we making in cooking class today?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Banana cookies, but we need to read the recipe first.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can I open it on the computer?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. I will write the steps on the board.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How do you spell the last word?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I am not sure. Let me use my eraser.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The teacher can help us after she checks the drinks.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay. Then we can start making breakfast.

units.titleZh: 食物與用餐 × 住家與物品
units.titleEn: Food and Meals & Home and Objects

passages.title: Food and Meals: First Reading
passages.text: It was hot after school, so my sister and I made ice cream in our kitchen. She mixed milk with ice while I poured juice into small cups. I added a little salt to the ice, but none went into the food. Mom set the dining room table and called our cousins. When they reached our house, we put away their coats and hats. Everyone enjoyed the cold dessert, and we saved one cup for Dad.

passages.title: Clothes and Looks: Second Reading
passages.text: Rain started while Lily was walking home in her new dress. She quickly put on her coat and hat, but her shoes still got wet. At the house, the telephone was ringing in the dining room. Lily answered it, and Dad asked her to warm dinner in the kitchen. She made a hot dog, poured some juice, and added a little salt to her soup. Later, she called Dad on her phone and said everything was ready.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What should we take to the picnic?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We have hot dogs and juice in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can we bring ice cream too?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It may melt before we reach the park.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then I will put some ice in this box.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good idea. Please wear your coat and hat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Should I call Amy on the phone?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. Tell her to meet us outside the house.

units.titleZh: 地點與交通 × 動作與日常
units.titleEn: Places and Transport & Actions and Routines

passages.title: Places and Transport: First Reading
passages.text: My cousin Jack came from America during the school holiday. We planned a day trip to a mountain town and took an early train. At the station, Jack saw many bicycles and asked if we could rent a bike. Mom said the road was too steep, so we rode a bus instead. A truck drove slowly in front of us, but we reached the town before lunch. Jack took photos and called the trip his favorite day in Taiwan.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: Second Reading
passages.text: Emma was learning to ride a bicycle in the park. Dad held the bike while she pushed the pedals, but she turned too quickly and fell into the grass. She began to cry, so Dad asked if she was hurt. Emma shook her head and tried again. Soon she could ride past a parked truck without help. Above her, a red kite flew across the sky. Dad called Mom and said, "Emma can ride by herself now!"

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How are we getting to the beach for our trip?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We can take the train at eight.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can we bring our bikes on it?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, but we need to ask at the station.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: My dad could drive us in his car instead.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The road may have many trucks this morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then I will call him and choose the train.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great. Let's meet by the bicycle shop.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: First Reading
passages.text: Our school held an autumn fair on Saturday. I joined the art team because they needed help with the signs. We worked together to make bright posters and waited for the paint to dry. Then we invited families into the hall. Some children tried a ball game, and others learned a simple dance. I helped a small boy kick the ball toward a basket. He missed twice, but his third try went in, so everyone cheered.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: Second Reading
passages.text: We found a wet puppy near our gate after a rainy walk. My sister took it inside while I called a neighbor for help. We used a towel to dry its fur and tried to make it drink some water. The puppy needed a quiet place to sleep, so we put a box by the door and waited. Soon the owner arrived from work. She kissed the puppy, thanked us, and invited us to visit them again.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Do you want to join our soccer practice?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, but I need help with my kicks.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I can work with you after school.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thanks. Should I invite Kevin too?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Sure. We can make two small teams.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let's wait until the field is dry.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay. I will take the ball home today.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great. We can try again tomorrow.

passages.title: Everyday English: First Reading
passages.text: Our English class made a pretend shop with play money. I put books on one table and wrote "one dollar" on each price card. Ben asked if we had any toy cars, so I looked under the table. "Oops, they are down here," I said. He was really happy and bought two. At the end, we counted the money together and packed everything up. We waved good-bye to our last customer and closed the shop.

passages.title: Everyday English: Second Reading
passages.text: The children were singing together for the school show. Amy stood up front, but she forgot one line and looked down at the floor. "Oh-oh," whispered Leo, but Amy remembered the words and kept going. The audience became quiet and listened. When the song ended, everyone clapped loudly. Amy smiled and said, "I really did it!" After the show, we picked up our bags, said goodbye to the teacher, and walked home together before dinner.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Oops, I dropped all the colored paper.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh-oh! Some pieces went under the desk.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are there any more down there?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Uh-uh, I think we found them all.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Really? Then let's put them up on the shelf.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We can carry the big box together.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks. I have to go now. Goodbye!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good-bye! See you at school tomorrow.
